prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: decision support for wildfire detection/suppression in dry, steep, windy wildland-urban interface terrain. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (alias Emberhall), primary operator interface for Duty Detection Officer, County Emergency Liaison and command staff; displays camera views, detection history, weather, map layers, status transitions. North Lookout Camera Mast (northern rim, long-range) and South Lookout Camera Mast (opposing viewshed, overlap); hardened power, lightning protection; video via licensed wireless links, cellular as degraded-mode path. North Lookout Camera Mast sends Thermal Spot Snippet after local processing finds candidate heat signature. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (alias Kestrel): graded pad near central ridge road; launch, recovery, charging, shelter, weather-rated enclosures, health monitoring, secure network termination; produces Battery Swap Ticket when its maintenance controller records a flight battery at replacement threshold. Drone Tasking Service: manages approved unmanned flight requests, records mission constraints, shows task status; not flight-release authority. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (alias Lantern): aggregates camera detections, weather, geospatial context, operator feedback into traceable advisory recommendations. Smoke Classifier Module: bounded component scoring plume likelihood, passes confidence values to analytics. Analytics retain event timing, source IDs, model versions, operator acknowledgments for review. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (alias Brindle): ingests station observations, forecast grids, quality checks; sends Wind Shift Bulletin on significant local wind change. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater: monitored radio-to-workstation bridge with recording/access controls. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console; East and West Retardant Loading Pumps; Crewline Mobile Tablet (mobile access). Organizations: local fire agencies, county emergency management, state wildland fire resources, aviation units, public safety partners. Actors: County Emergency Liaison; Duty Detection Officer (alias Orion), monitors cues, requests verification, recommends escalation; Air Attack Supervisor; Tanker Base Manager; Helitack Crew Leader; Drone Pilot Operator (uses Drone Tasking Service to review routes, dock status, constraints before procedural coordination). States: Suspected ignition, Confirmed Ignition State, Airspace Restricted State. Detection support ends when authorized role accepts, rejects or requests verification. Requirements: Orion recommends Confirmed Ignition State only when observations/procedures support it; no autonomous dispatch, command, or direct control of aircraft, vehicles, pumps, cameras, drones, crews; command authority stays with incident command;

New part:
S047: Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console supports the Air Attack Supervisor and Tanker Base Manager by presenting aircraft coordination data, loading status, and mission notes relevant to suppression support.
S048: East Retardant Loading Pump and West Retardant Loading Pump are represented in the site layout as monitored ground assets whose readiness and fault indications are visible to authorized operations staff.
S049: Crewline Mobile Tablet provides the Helitack Crew Leader with field access to assigned incident context, map references, and updates that have been approved for mobile distribution.
S050: Across the site, network segmentation, time synchronization, equipment health checks, and audit logging are treated as baseline infrastructure rather than optional add-ons.
S051: The detection workflow begins when the North Lookout Camera Mast, South Lookout Camera Mast, or Horizon Ridge Drone Dock provides an observation that may indicate a new ignition.
S052: Each observation is time stamped, georeferenced, and associated with equipment status before it is evaluated as operational evidence.
S053: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine receives the observation context and normalizes image, thermal, and weather attributes into a common event record.
S054: Smoke indications are initially assessed for plume texture, persistence, motion, and contrast against the background terrain.
S055: Thermal cues are treated as supporting evidence unless they persist across sequential frames or align with a visible smoke indication.
S056: The Smoke Classifier Module produces the Ridge Shadow Mask when terrain-shadow conditions could otherwise inflate a smoke confidence score.
S057: The analytics score is not considered a declaration of fire, because atmospheric glare, dust, vehicle exhaust, and cloud shadow can produce similar signatures.
S058: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node provides local wind, humidity, temperature, and stability context that helps determine whether an indication is plausible for active combustion.
S059: When the automated confidence level exceeds the screening threshold, the Caldera Incident Command Portal opens a triage case for human review.
S060: The Duty Detection Officer reviews the triage case, compares current imagery with recent frames, and checks whether the indication is growing, drifting, or disappearing.
S061: The Duty Detection Officer may request a fresh pan, tilt, or zoom view from the nearest fixed camera when the initial frame is ambiguous.
S062: If terrain, smoke column height, or occlusion prevents a clear fixed-camera view, the Drone Tasking Service may prepare a verification task for the Horizon Ridge Drone Dock.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
